findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded directly in the Lambda environment variables in source control. Anyone with read access to the repo, the Lambda console, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve them and impersonate that IAM principal; the function should use its execution role instead.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which hold credentials here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key, providing no customer-controlled key policy or separation of access for these sensitive values.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unaddressed.
